prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals and commitments (ideological framing removed)

- Tax, pay and family support
  - Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main self‑employed NI by end of Parliament; no rises in income tax, VAT or corporation tax.
  - Triple Lock Plus: state pension and a new age‑related personal allowance rise by the highest of inflation, earnings or 2.5%; maintain existing pensioner benefits; no new taxes on pensions.
  - Child Benefit to be assessed on household income, tapering from £120,000 to £160,000.
  - 30 hours free childcare from nine months to school start by Sept 2025; expand wraparound childcare by 2026.
  - Maintain National Living Wage at two‑thirds of median earnings.

- Business, innovation and trade
  - Maintain full expensing and consider extending to leasing; 10‑point SME plan (rates relief, prompt payment enforcement, open finance, regional mutual banks, Invest in Women Fund).
  - Public R&D to £22bn a year; scale AI compute; Advanced Manufacturing Plan; strengthen Catapults; Mansion House reforms.
  - Complete FTAs with India and GCC; implement CPTPP; maintain TCA without CJEU alignment; NHS and food standards excluded from trade deals.

- Infrastructure and planning
  - Reallocate £36bn from HS2 phase 2 to regional transport (roads, rail, buses, potholes); nationwide gigabit by 2030; standalone 5G in all populated areas; automated vehicles enabled.
  - Speed up consents and environmental assessments; limit unmerited judicial reviews.

- Welfare and work
  - Reform disability benefits and assessments; overhaul fit notes to specialist work/health professionals; tighten Work Capability Assessment.
  - Accelerate Universal Credit rollout; tougher sanctions after 12 months; new Fraud Bill to strengthen DWP powers; support unpaid carers.

- Education and youth
  - Mandatory National Service at 18 (paid competitive military year or part‑time civic service).
  - 100,000 extra apprenticeships funded by closing poor‑outcome degree courses; introduce Advanced British Standard (16‑19).
  - Statutory school‑day mobile phone ban; expand SEN places; Family Hubs in every local authority.

- Health and social care
  - NHS spending to rise above inflation; recruit 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors; expand Pharmacy First; 250 GP surgeries built/modernised; 50 more Community Diagnostic Centres.
  - £3.4bn tech plan: NHS App as single front door, AI adoption, Federated Data Platform; reduce managers by 5,500.
  - Dental Recovery Plan (more appointments, contract reform, service requirement for new dentists); women’s health strategy; Tobacco and Vapes Bill; expand mental health support (school teams to 100%).

- Immigration and borders
  - Legal, binding annual cap on work and family visas, voted by Parliament and reducing each year.
  - Monthly removals to Rwanda; implement Illegal Migration Act; pursue returns deals; seek international asylum rule changes.
  - Health checks and higher charges/insurance where needed; raise Skilled Worker thresholds; restrict dependants.

- Defence, security and foreign policy
  - Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; at least £10bn for munitions; 5% of defence budget for R&D plus 2% for exploitation; procurement reform.
  - Long‑term support for Ukraine; Veterans’ Bill and Office for Veterans’ Affairs maintained.

- Policing, justice and protests
  - 8,000 extra neighbourhood police; Martyn’s Law; hotspot policing; tougher sentences for serious crimes and domestic homicides; expand fraud measures; clearer protest enforcement powers.

- Energy and net zero
  - Annual North Sea oil and gas licensing; maintain windfall tax (with investment allowances) to 2028‑29.
  - New gas power stations; treble offshore wind; deliver CCS clusters; approve two SMR fleets within 100 days; progress Wylfa.
  - Keep green levies lower than 2023; maintain price cap; Pumpwatch; £6bn for home energy efficiency plus universal vouchers; onshore wind with local consent; protect best farmland for solar; no fracking.

- Housing
  - 1.6m homes; lift nutrient neutrality barriers with mitigation fees; brownfield fast‑track in 20 largest cities; densify inner London; development corporations; SME builder support.
  - Permanent FTB Stamp Duty threshold at £425k; new Help to Buy; CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants; leasehold reform; Renters Reform (abolish Section 21 after court changes); manage holiday lets; rough sleeping plan.

- Transport and drivers
  - Backing Drivers Bill: ban local road pricing; reverse ULEZ expansion; community votes for 20mph/LTNs; extend £2 bus fare cap for the Parliament.
  - Rail Reform Bill to create Great British Railways; nationwide contactless; no new smart motorways; parking and pavement parking reforms.

- Law on sex and gender
  - Clarify in law that Equality Act “sex” means biological sex; one legal sex per person; implement Cass Review, ban private prescription of puberty blockers; single‑sex accommodation in NHS.

- Farming, fisheries, rural and environment
  - Increase UK‑wide farming budget by £1bn over the Parliament; legal food security target; fast‑track farm infrastructure; 50% public procurement local/higher‑standard food.
  - Replicate £100m UK Seafood Fund; seek more inshore opportunities.
  - Maintain record flood defence funding; Plan for Water (tougher penalties, river recovery network, regulatory reform); tree/peat programmes; new National Park; deposit return scheme; limit new incinerators.

- Union and levelling up
  - Protect internal market; Intertrade UK; extend Shared Prosperity Fund three years; more town endowments; support Freeports/Investment Zones; targeted measures for Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland (e.g., North Wales Main Line electrification, Wylfa, A75 improvements, Port Talbot support, Windsor Framework delivery).
